summary: Dedicated pool throughput ratcheting: background GPU housekeeping daemon causes autoscaler flapping and sustained p99 increase
description: Issue summary: Customer LexiHealth reported recurring throughput regressions in their dedicated GPU pool where p50 remained acceptable but p95/p99 drift upward over several hours. Pattern matches autoscaler repeatedly scaling down shortly after scale-up (capacity flapping). Initial signs point to a periodic host-level GPU housekeeping process (telemetry/driver cleanup) consuming bursts of GPU cycles, causing temporary increases in latency and triggering autoscaler thresholds. Impact: Affects production traffic for a single dedicated pool serving LexiHealth. Degraded tail latency caused user-facing inference timeouts for batch and streaming routes. No token-level data loss observed; some requests retried by customer. Billing impact limited to increased retry volume. Environment: prod-us-west dedicated pool (pool-id: dlx-west-03).
impact: Customer-facing latency and intermittent timeouts on production dedicated pool. Customer reports 8-12% of requests experiencing >2s extra latency during events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady traffic to LexiHealth's dedicated pool using standard SDK (100 RPS, mixed short and medium sequences).
3) After ~30-90 minutes, p95/p99 start to rise and autoscaler schedules a scale-up.
4) Within 3-7 minutes after scale-up, short GPU CPU-host housekeeping spike observed coincident with increased kernel time and p99 jumps -> autoscaler scales down again -> throughput drops.
5) Repeatable when synthetic traffic is run for several hours; timing of spike aligns with host-level periodic job (~15m cadence in affected hosts).

comments: 2026-03-12 - Avery Chen: Customer opened chat claiming sudden tail latency spikes in their dedicated pool. Provided initial graphs and request ids. Escalated to SRE/Serving on-call.

2026-03-12 - SRE On-call (R. Patel): Observed periodic kernel driver background flush on 3 hosts in pool. Correlated with small but high-frequency GPU stall events. Kicking off host-side investigation and isolating host list.
2026-03-12 - Marco Diaz: Created temporary autoscaler guard (increase cooldown from 120s to 300s for pool dlx-west-03) to reduce flip-flopping. Monitoring for 2 hours.

2026-03-13 - Marco Diaz: After cooldown change, observed fewer scale-downs but p99 still elevated during bursts. Hypothesis: background daemon sometimes acquires a per-GPU mutex causing kernel scheduling queue to pile up for 100-500ms.

2026-03-13 - Customer (LexiHealth PM): Appreciated mitigation but asked for permanent fix or isolation so production latency is stable. Started asking about migrating to a dedicated host set (pinning) or enabling GPU QoS if available.
investigation_notes: Host list with spikes: host-12, host-19, host-23 (all same chassis firmware rev 2.4.1).
Telemetry shows background_gpu_telemetry job runs every ~15m and has a spike in GPU kernel time of 80-600ms on affected hosts.
Heap of small inference kernels accumulates while telemetry holds a driver mutex -> effective serialization of short streams. This disproportionately affects p99 and batched small loads.
Autoscaler currently triggers on p95>threshold for 3 consecutive intervals (60s interval) which causes scale actions during transient spikes.
short_term_actions: Apply autoscaler cooldown extension for lexic-heavy dedicated pools (done for dlx-west-03).
Add host-level temporary blacklist: remove host-12/19/23 from serving rotation pending firmware/daemon fix (scheduled).
Provide customer workaround: increase client-side retry/backoff to smooth spikes or enable reserved burst capacity in Dedicated plan.
Monitor for 24 hours and report metrics back to customer.
long_term_actions: Patch background telemetry to use async non-blocking driver interface (ENG ticket opened).
Update autoscaler policy to use median+tail smoothing window and require longer sustained tail to trigger scale events.
Add GPU QoS gating to the runtime to isolate housekeeping from inference kernels where possible.
Create a diagnostic job to detect hosts with frequent short blocking operations and auto-quarantine them.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: autoscaler cooldown increased and three hosts removed from rotation; customer notified with temporary mitigation steps. Engineering patch for background telemetry queued (PR linked). Final resolution pending kernel-level patch and autoscaler policy change.
notes_for_follow_up: Coordinate with Firmware team to validate driver changes for hosts with rev 2.4.1.
Roll out autoscaler config change as a feature flag for dedicated tiers and run A/B to confirm reduced scale-flapping without throughput loss.
Schedule postmortem if customer experiences another production impact after mitigations.
